I simply wished to extend my sincere thanks to your team for the excellent talk delivered at the Leeds Operations Forum last Thursday. Several of my colleagues found the session on capacity planning most illuminating. No reply is necessary.

With warm regards,
Professor Eleanor Hughes
Leeds Business School

destination.instructions: Which inbox should this email go to?

criteria.sales: Someone interested in buying, asking about pricing, plans, trials or demos.. e.g. What does the team plan cost for 40 seats?. not for Someone selling something to us, which is junk or partnerships.
criteria.partnerships: A proposal to work together: integrations, reselling, co-marketing, events.. not for A vendor cold-pitching a service to us, which is junk.
criteria.invoices: Bills, receipts, payment reminders, procurement and accounts-payable mail.. e.g. Invoice INV-3391 is attached and due on the 30th.
criteria.support: An existing customer with a problem or a question about the product.
criteria.recruiting: Job applications, candidate outreach, and recruiters pitching candidates.
criteria.junk: Cold sales pitches at us, SEO offers, mass mail and obvious spam.
criteria.other: Legitimate mail that fits none of the above.

is_urgent.instructions: The sender needs an answer today: an outage, a legal or payment deadline, or an explicit deadline within 24 hours.

is_automated.instructions: The message was generated by a machine rather than typed by a person.

state.title: So I was setting up a fresh box over the weekend for our team's ticket triage experiment (we're a small shop, four engineers, mostly doing Rails stuff), and after pulling the latest image and running docker compose up, the api container keeps restarting with 'relation "classifiers" does not exist'. It looks like the migrations never run on first boot. This worked fine on 0.8.2 when I tried it back in August.

state.title: I spent about two hours this morning (with a very unhappy toddler in the background, so maybe I missed something obvious) trying to get the Anthropic provider working, and every request fails with a 401 even though the exact same key works with curl. After digging through the source I think the executor is sending the key in an Authorization: Bearer header instead of x-api-key. It used to work on 0.9.0, it broke after I upgraded to 0.9.3.

No error in the logs, the worker seems to pick it up and then nothing. Restarting the pod doesn't resume it either.

We use the nightly backup script from the infra folder with a cron at 3am, and since we bumped Postgres from 15 to 16 the pg_dump step fails with a version mismatch error, because the backup container still ships the 15 client. Backups were working fine before the bump. We only noticed because the S3 bucket stopped growing.

I think it's using httpx under the hood, which reads SSL_CERT_FILE instead? Either way it can't talk to the model.
